quarterly_data.signal: CEO split the GaN roadmap into two supply models. Lateral GaN (GaN-on-Silicon) is sourced through partners: 'We have announced a partnership with Innoscience and a partnership with GlobalFoundries... We are partnering with very strong partners externally to get access to the GaN-on-Silicon devices,' while onsemi keeps the control and driver silicon internal on Treo; the combined go-to-market was announced at PCIM. Vertical GaN is fully organic (plus a small tuck-in acquisition for IP) and is built in onsemi's own fab in Syracuse, New York: 'we have the fab. It is up and running. We are sampling, so we have physical samples at customers on their boards being tested.' He claims onsemi is the only company in the world manufacturing vertical GaN today and that competitors would have to work around its patents, and positions it as complementary to silicon carbide for size- and density-constrained sockets.

The 'AI halo' inside industrial was quantified: 'Our energy infrastructure business is growing 40% year-on-year, and that secular side of the business, I think, posted a 25% sequential.' The secular part (energy storage, energy infrastructure, ADAS, medical) is about 60% of onsemi's industrial market. onsemi says it is number one in energy storage systems and is extending into solid state transformers, where the content is entirely incremental: 'historically, transformers have had no electronics content. When we go to solid state, that's all incremental' for onsemi. Management frames this as the build-out feeding the 800V transition and keeps it in industrial, separate from AI data center revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: energy infrastructure +40% year-on-year; secular industrial +25% sequential; secular ~60% of total industrial

quarterly_data.signal: Treo detail behind the margin bridge: it is a 65-nanometer BCD mixed-signal analog platform that runs up to 90 volt - 'there is no other technology or no other peer today that is able to deliver a 65-nanometer up to 90 volt' - which lets onsemi integrate high voltage monolithically with analog. Design cycles on Treo are six to nine months versus two years before. First Treo products are already shipping, including 10BASE-T1S automotive Ethernet (a market onsemi historically was not in) now in automotive production, plus medical, industrial and AI data center ramps. 'The margin profile on Treo-based products is in that 60%-70% gross margin' and management has targeted 2030 revenue of $1 billion for the franchise.
quarterly_data.figure: Treo 65-nanometer up to 90 volt; six to nine months vs two years design cycle; 60%-70% gross margin; $1 billion revenue in 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Automotive framed with numbers the call did not give: 'We expect automotive to grow about 6% or so year-on-year' against a flat-to-slightly-down SAAR, and over the last five years (end of 2019 to beginning of 2026) onsemi's automotive revenue grew 72%, 'a 9.5% CAGR over a five-year period.' New content drivers: plug-in hybrids are moving from IGBT/silicon power to silicon carbide as OEMs push 100-mile range - 'we have already have two design in China and North America for a plug-in hybrid with silicon carbide' - and the zonal/software-defined-vehicle architecture products (10BASE-T1S Ethernet, smart power at every zone) start ramping this year.
quarterly_data.figure: automotive ~6% year-on-year; 72% growth over five years (9.5% CAGR); two plug-in hybrid silicon carbide designs (China and North America)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO put boundaries on capacity and inventory. Distributor channel inventory is at the target 10 to 11 weeks and onsemi holds stock back ('They would take more inventory if we'd ship it to them'); balance-sheet inventory came down 8 days to 67 days, with the bridge inventory from the earlier fab divestitures taking 'a couple more years to bleed through it all.' CapEx stays in mid-single-digit percentage intensity 'for several years': 'Our revenue has to get to about 30% higher than where it is today for us even to think about adding capacity,' and about 35% of production is managed outside, which onsemi loads last. 'We're not breaking ground on a new fab anytime soon.'
quarterly_data.figure: channel inventory 10 to 11 weeks; inventory down 8 days to 67 days; revenue must be ~30% higher before adding capacity; ~35% of production managed outside

quarterly_data.signal: Next catalyst: CEO pointed to onsemi's Analyst Day on September 16th for the detailed TAM and content disclosure across end markets, specifically the energy / AI-halo opportunity outside the data center walls. CFO declined a preview: 'You must be present to win.'
